questions.q: Who is the protagonist of the story and what is her name?
questions.a: The protagonist is the grandmother, named Krishtakka (also called Avva). She is a 62-year-old woman living in a village in North Karnataka who cannot read. A wrong answer (e.g., "the granddaughter") confuses the narrator with the protagonist — the granddaughter narrates the story but Krishtakka is the central character whose journey drives the plot.

questions.q: What event triggers Krishtakka's decision to learn to read?
questions.a: When the granddaughter (narrator) went away for a week to a neighboring village for a wedding, Krishtakka could not read the latest episode of Kashi Yatre herself. She felt helpless and dependent, which triggered her decision to learn to read. A wrong answer (e.g., "she wanted to visit Kashi") confuses the magazine serial's plot with Krishtakka's motivation — Kashi Yatre is what she wanted to read, not where she wanted to go.

questions.q: In 3-4 sentences, summarize the key events of the story in chronological order.
questions.a: Krishtakka, an illiterate grandmother in a North Karnataka village, depended on her granddaughter to read her the weekly serial Kashi Yatre. When the granddaughter was away for a week, Krishtakka realized her helplessness and decided to learn to read at age 62. She set a Saraswati Puja deadline, practiced daily, and by the deadline could read Kashi Yatre independently. She then touched her granddaughter's feet as guru dakshina, honoring her as her teacher. A wrong answer that adds analysis (e.g., "this shows the power of determination") is not a summary — it is interpretation.

questions.q: What is the significance of the Saraswati Puja deadline in the story?
questions.a: The Saraswati Puja deadline is the date by which Krishtakka committed to learning the alphabet and reading independently. Saraswati Puja is a festival honoring Saraswati, the goddess of learning, making the deadline symbolically meaningful. It creates narrative tension (will she succeed in time?) and marks the resolution when she achieves her goal. A wrong answer (e.g., "it is just a festival") ignores the narrative function of the deadline as a structural device that creates suspense and resolution.

questions.q: What is the guru dakshina moment and why is it significant to the plot?
questions.a: Guru dakshina is the traditional offering a student gives to a teacher at the end of learning. In the story, Krishtakka touches her granddaughter's feet as guru dakshina after learning to read, reversing their roles — the grandmother honors the granddaughter as her teacher. This is the climax and resolution of the story, completing the narrative arc from dependence to independence and from student-teacher to guru-shishya relationship. A wrong answer (e.g., "it is a gift") misses the cultural and narrative significance of the role reversal.

questions.q: A student writes: "The story is about how a grandmother learned to read and it is very inspiring." Evaluate this as a summary and suggest two improvements.
questions.a: This is not a proper summary — it is too vague and includes an opinion ("inspiring"). Improvements: (1) Add specific events: mention Kashi Yatre, the granddaughter's absence, the Saraswati Puja deadline, and the guru dakshina. (2) Remove the opinion — a summary states what happened, not whether it is inspiring. A better version: "Krishtakka, an illiterate grandmother in North Karnataka, depended on her granddaughter to read Kashi Yatre. When the granddaughter was away, Krishtakka felt helpless and decided to learn. She set a Saraswati Puja deadline, practiced daily, and achieved independent reading, then honored her granddaughter as guru dakshina."

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A story summary is a concise, objective restatement of a narrative's main events, characters, setting, conflict, and resolution in the student's own words, preserving ______ order and omitting minor details, personal opinions, and analysis.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have two minutes to tell a younger sibling the entire story of "How I Taught My ______ to Read" — what would you say?
Fill in the blank: For "How I Taught My Grandmother to Read" by Sudha Murty, the summary captures Krishtakka's journey from illiteracy to independent reading at age ______.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can write a 100-150 word summary of "How I Taught My Grandmother to Read" that identifies the protagonist (Krishtakka), setting (North Karnataka village), central conflict (illiteracy and dependence), key events in sequence (listening to Kashi Yatre, narrator's absence, decision to learn, daily practice, Saraswati Puja deadline.
